description_en: Adikālī Temple is an important Śāktapīṭhalocated in Baniyā̃ Village, Naikap (Nayā̃ Bhañjyāṅ), within Chandragiri Municipality. The shrine is situated on the highest rocky outcrop of the area, incorporating an ancient natural cave, a setting that confers both natural sanctity and historical significance on the site. Thepīṭhawas established directly upon this rock, and the temple structure was subsequently constructed atop it. To the south of the temple lies the Newar settlement known as Banthachā, whose residents have long venerated Ādikālī as theiriṣṭadevatā. Records preserved at the Guṭhī Saṃsthān refer to this sacred site by names such as “Naikāpa Ānandeśvara Indreśvara Ādikālī” and “Naikāpa Śrī Ānandeśvara Bhakteśvara Ādyakālī,” underscoring its layered religious identity and regional importance (S. Maharjana 2082 VS, 48). Access to the temple is provided by a flight of steps ascending from the east, and remnants of ancient rock formations remain visible throughout the temple complex. At the highest point stands an aniconic (amūrta) stone revered as Ādikālī, upon which the temple itself has been erected.Architecturally, the temple is a single-storeyed, east-facing structure. The roof is clad with copper sheets, and thegajurais likewise made of copper. Upon the large stone identified with Ādikālī, a metal image of the goddess has been installed. Near this image an inscription is visible, and beneath it two metal lions have been placed. The temple entrance is fitted with an iron door. On the southern side of the temple are installed an image of Gaṇeśa and a mask-like representation of Bhairava. Immediately to the west stands akuṭībelonging to the Aghorī ascetic tradition, whose members continue to reside there and perform ritual worship of Ādikālī.The site has long been associated with renouncers such as Aghorīsannyāsīs, who maintain the tradition of installing and worshipping Kālī according to Vedic ritual procedures. Although records of thekhaṭa-jātrānote that Svāmī Lalitānanda was residing at this site prior to 1968 CE (2025 VS), no definitive historical evidence has yet been found regarding the original establishment of the Ādikālī Pīṭha or its founder. Svāmī Lalitānanda, an ascetic of this lineage, was provided with a residentialkuṭīand a cowshed for his sustenance. An official document issued by the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna in 1938 CE (1995 VS) records alālamoharagranting Śrī 108 Lalitānanda Svāmī formal permission to reside at this sacred site (S. Maharjana 2082 VS, 72). Following his death in 1968 CE (2025 VS), his disciples have continued to inhabit thekuṭī, conducting the daily worship (nityapūjā),ārati, and other ritual activities in accordance with the establishedguru–śiṣyalineage.Over time, the surrounding settlement developed through migration from nearby ancient villages. In the absence of a distinctive local festival tradition, inhabitants who had migrated from Kīrtipur observed the Sāt Gāule Jātrā, while those from Balambu continued to celebrate the Mahālakṣmī Jātrā of Balambu. A significant transformation occurred in 1984 CE (2040 VS), when representatives of threeguthis based in Banthachā convened and entered into a written agreement to institute an annualkhaṭa-jātrāof Ādikālī. In accordance with this agreement, the festival has since been celebrated every year from eighth of bright fortnight of Mangsira to the tenth. These dates coincide with the well-known Sāta Gāũle Jātrā, and the Ādikālī Jātrā is observed in coordinated alignment with that regional festival.The temple and its precincts have undergone continuous conservation and development through donations and collective efforts by local residents, individuals, and institutions across different periods. In 1929 CE (1986 VS), local residents of Baniyā̃ Gāũ, together with Svāmī Lalitānanda, donated a bell to the goddess. In 1986 CE (2042 VS), Naikap Ward No. 5 and Kāpikā Rānā Magara provided financial assistance for the purchase of images of Gaṇeśa, Ādikālī, and Bhairava, for the construction of a building to house the festival palanquins (khaṭa), and for the management of the annual procession, including the establishment of an endowment fund of NPR 15,000. Further improvements to the temple and its surroundings were carried out in 1999 CE (2055 VS) with support from various organizations and individuals. In 2004 CE (2060 VS), the Ādikālī Temple Area Construction and Conservation Committee completed major renovation works through donations collected from multiple locations and patrons. In the most recent phase, in 2019 CE (2075 VS), additional financial contributions from institutions and individuals enabled the construction of a truss-supported structure with a copper roof, further strengthening and securing the temple complex.Thus, the present form of the Ādikālī Pīṭha and temple precinct is the cumulative result of sustained ritual continuity, ascetic stewardship, community devotion, and periodic acts of patronage extending across more than a century.
description_ne: पीठमा अघोरी सन्यासीहरूले वैदिक विधिअनुसार पूजा गर्ने परम्परा रहेको छ भने हरेक बर्ष मंसिर शुक्ल अष्टमीदेखि दशमीसम्म मनाइने आदिकालीको जात्रा विसं २०४० (सन् १९८४) देखि मनाउन थालिएको थियो ।आदिकाली मन्दिर चन्द्रागिरि नगरपालिकाको नैकाप (नयाँ भन्ज्याङ), बानिया गाउँमा अवस्थित एक महत्वपूर्ण शाक्त–पीठ हो । यस भेगको सबैभन्दा उचाइ भएको चट्टानी भाग र त्यहाँ रहेको प्राचीन गुफासहितको स्थानमा आदिकालीको पीठ स्थापना गरिएको छ । पीठ अवस्थित चट्टानकै माथि मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको छ, जसले यस स्थललाई प्राकृतिकरूपमा पवित्रता र ऐतिहासिक महत्त्व प्रदान गरेको छ ।मन्दिरको दक्षिणतर्फ ‘बन्थचा’ नामक नेवार बस्ती रहेको छ । बन्थचाका नेवार समुदायले आदिकालीलाई आफ्नो इष्टदेवीको रूपमा पूजाआराधना गर्दै आएका छन् । गुठी संस्थानमा प्राप्त विभिन्न अभिलेखहरूमा यस पीठलाई “नैकाप आनन्देश्वर इन्द्रेश्वर आदिकाली” तथा “नैकाप श्री आनन्देश्वर भक्तेश्वर आद्यकाली” नामले उल्लिखित गरिएको पाइन्छ (S. Maharjana VS 2082, p. 48) । जसले यस क्षेत्रको धार्मिक महत्वलाई अझ प्रष्ट पार्दछ । मन्दिरसम्म पुग्नका लागि पूर्वतर्फ सिँढी निर्माण गरिएको छ। मन्दिर परिसरमा अहिले पनि ठाउँ–ठाउँमा प्राचीन चट्टानहरू देख्न सकिन्छ । सबैभन्दा अग्लो स्थानमा रहेको अमूर्त (अनाकार) ढुङ्गालाई आदिकालीका रूपमा प्रतिष्ठा गरिएको छ, र यही चट्टानमाथि मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको हो ।मन्दिर एकतले संरचनामा पूर्वाभिमुख भएर निर्मित छ । छानामा तामाका पाता प्रयोग गरिएको छ तथा गजुर पनि तामाकै बनेको छ । आदिकाली मानेको ठूलो ढुङ्गामाथि धातुको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । मूर्तिको नजिकै एउटा अभिलेख (inscription) देख्न सकिन्छ, र मूर्तिको तलपट्टि धातुकै दुईवटा सिंह स्थापना गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको ढोका फलामको बनेको छ । मन्दिरको दक्षिण भागमा गणेशको मूर्ति र भैरवको मुखाकृति स्थापना गरिएको छ। मन्दिरको ठीक पश्चिमपट्टि सन्यासी (अघोरी) सम्प्रदायको कुटी रहेको छ, जहाँ अघोरी अनुयायीहरूले आदिकालीको पूजा गर्दै आएका छन् ।विभिन्न कालखण्डमा मन्दिर र यसको आसपासको क्षेत्रमा स्थानीय समुदाय, व्यक्तित्व तथा संघ–संस्थाहरूको उल्लेख्य सहयोग र दानबाट निरन्तर रूपमा संरक्षण, मर्मत तथा विकास हुँदै आएको देखिन्छ । विसं १९८६ (सन् १९२९) बानियाँ गाउँका स्थानीय र स्वामी ललितानन्दले देवीलाई घण्टा चढाएर थियो । विसं २०४२ (सन् १९८६) मा नैकाप वडा नं. ५ तथा कापिका राना मगरले वार्षिक यात्रा सञ्चालनका लागि गणेश, आदिकाली र भैरवका मूर्ति खरिद, खट राख्न भवन निर्माण गर्न आर्थिक सहयोग गर्नुका साथै जात्रा व्यवस्थापनका लागि पन्ध्र हजार रूपैयाँ अक्षयकोष स्थापना गरिएको थियो । त्यस्तै, विसं २०५५ (सन् १९९९) मा विभिन्न संघ–संस्था र व्यक्तिहरूको सहयोगमा मन्दिर तथा क्षेत्र सुधारको कार्य सम्पन्न गरियो भने विसं २०६० (सन् २००४) मा आदिकाली मन्दिर परिसर निर्माण तथा संरक्षण समितिले विभिन्न स्थान र व्यक्तिबाट संकलित सहयोगमार्फत मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार सम्पन्न गरियो । यसरी, आदिकाली मन्दिर क्षेत्र समय–समयमा प्राप्त दान, भक्ति र सामुदायिक सहभागिताबाट आजको स्वरूपमा विकसित भएको हो । पछिल्लो चरणमा, विसं २०७५ (सन् २०१९) मा मन्दिर तामाको छाना सहितको ट्रस संरचना निर्माण गर्न विभिन्न संघ–संस्था र व्यक्तिबाट प्राप्त आर्थिक सहयोगले मन्दिरको संरचना अझ मजबुत र सुरक्षित बनेको देखिन्छ ।अघोरी सन्यासीहरूले यस स्थलमा काली स्थापना गरी वैदिक विधिअनुसार पूजा गर्ने परम्परा निरन्तर चलाउँदै आएका छन् । खट जात्राको अभिलेखमा यस स्थानमा स्वामी ललितानन्द विसं २०२५ (सन् १९६८) अघिदेखि बसोबास गर्दै आएको कुरा उल्लेख भएको भएतापनि आदिकालीको स्थापना कहिले र कसले गर्यो भन्ने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण प्राप्त छैन । स्वामी ललितानन्द नामका सन्यासीलाई बसोबासका लागि कुटी र गौशाला समेत व्यवस्थापन गरी दिइएको थियो । गुठी संस्थानले विसं १९९५ (सन् १९३८) मा लालमोहर जारी गरी श्री १०८ ललितानन्द स्वामीलाई यस स्थानमा आधिकारिक रूपमा बस्न अनुमति दिएको अभिलेख पाइन्छ (S. Maharjana VS 2082, p. 72) । विसं २०२५ (सन् १९६८) मा उनको निधनपछि गुरु–शिष्य परम्परा अनुसार उनका शिष्यहरूले नै कुटीमा बस्दै पीठको नित्यपूजा, आरती तथा अन्य धार्मिक क्रियाकलाप सञ्चालन गर्दै आएका छन् । यस क्षेत्रमा नजिकका प्राचीन बस्तीहरूबाट बसाइँ–सराई आएपछि बस्ती विकसित भएको मानिन्छ । आफ्नै मौलिक जात्रा परम्परा नहुँदा कीर्तिपुरबाट आएका मानिसहरूले सात गाउले जात्रा तथा बलम्बुबाट आएकाले बलम्बुको महालक्ष्मी जात्रा मनाउने प्रचलन थियो । विसं २०४० (सन् १९८४) मा बन्थचामा रहेको तीनवटा गुठीको मानिसहरू भेला भई आदिकालीको खट जात्रा गर्ने लिखित सम्झौता गर्दछन् । त्यही सम्झौता अनुसार हरेक बर्ष मंसिर शुक्ल अष्टमीदेखि दशमीसम्म जात्रा संचालन गर्दै आइरहेको छ । यस तिथिमा प्रसिद्ध ‘सात गाउले जात्रा’ पर्ने गर्दछ । यहाँको आदिकाली जात्रा सात गाउले जात्रासँग समन्वय गरी मनाइने गरेको पाइन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Near the large stone identified as the seat of Ādikālī, an inscription has been erected. However, due to severe weathering, the contents of the inscription are now largely illegible.
On one occasion during a ritual observance, local residents of Bāniyā̃ Village, together with Svāmī Lalitānanda, offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) to the goddess.

The continuation of the Khaṭa Jātrā is based on a written agreement prepared after consultations among the residents of Bāniyā̃ Village, Banthacā Tole, and the concernedguṭhīs, and has been observed annually from the eighth of bright fortnight of Maṅsira to the 10th.

For the organization of the annual procession, Naikap Ward No. 5 provided support for the purchase of three metal images—Gaṇeśa, Ādikālī, and Bhairava—and for the construction of a building to house thekhaṭas. The remaining expenses were borne by Kāpikā Rānā Magara, in memory of her late father Śrī Nara Bahādura Rānā Magara. In addition, she established a permanent endowment (akṣaya-kośa) of fifteen thousand rupees to ensure the continued operation of thejātrā.
With the assistance of various organizations and individuals, improvement works were carried out in the Ādikālī Temple and its surrounding area.

Restoration efforts were undertaken by the Ādikālī Temple Area Construction and Conservation Committee, which successfully completed the renovation of the temple through support collected from multiple institutions and private donors.
Among notable donations, Mohanalāla Rāī, son of Dila Bahādura Rāī—the grandson of Jaramāna Rāī, an early settler of New Naikap—along with his family, offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) to the deity.

In the most recent phase of development, financial contributions and voluntary labor donated by various organizations and individuals enabled the installation of copper roofing on the temple and the construction of a truss structure, thereby strengthening the building and enhancing its long-term structural safety.
